summary: Tarnovell head-office cross-sell deck (June 2026) for BD leads across the group. Reuses Quenverell's 'Bioinformatics for drug discovery' slide, maps the group's service lines, and uses Corvenlea as the worked example: it bought chemistry from Vellacombe as Corvenlea Pharma, DMPK from Merrivoss as Corvenlea Ltd and stability work from Westravelle as Corvenlea Pharmaceuticals plc, but never biology, bioinformatics or formulation.

properties.title: One Tarnovell: cross-selling across the group
properties.subject: Cross-sell

slides.title: One Tarnovell: cross-selling across the group
slides.subtitle: Commercial workstream | One Group, Many Practices | June 2026

slides.title: Why this matters
bullets: Most clients buy from one legacy firm only
Each firm's CRM knows its own clients under its own names
We lose opportunities we already have the relationship for
Goal for 2026-27: every top-30 account reviewed for white space

slides.title: Bioinformatics for drug discovery
bullets: Turns large biological datasets into decisions at each stage of a programme

bullets.text: Target identification: rank disease-linked genes from transcriptomics, genetics and curated pathways
Target validation support: expression evidence in the right tissue, cell type and patients to guide functional testing
Mechanism of action: pathway responses to compound treatment
Biomarker candidates: response signatures and monitoring markers for validation

bullets: Reproducible analyses with documented data acceptance
Offered by Quenverell Computational; easy to add to chemistry or biology proposals
slides.notes: Slide reused from the Quenverell 2025 capability deck with their agreement. Use it in any pitch where the client has omics data but no in-house team.

slides.title: Where to look for white space
bullets: Clients buying chemistry but not biology
Biology clients with no DMPK partner
Late-stage clients with no stability or formulation provider
Any client whose name changed: check all legacy CRMs

slides.title: Worked example: Corvenlea
slides.subtitle: One client, three names, three firms

slides.title: Corvenlea across the group
slides.notes: Same company: Corvenlea Pharma became Corvenlea Ltd, then listed in 2019 as Corvenlea Pharmaceuticals plc. Three CRMs held three separate accounts until the client identity bridge linked them.

slides.title: Corvenlea: what they have never bought from us
bullets: Bought: chemistry (Vellacombe)
Bought: DMPK (Merrivoss)
Bought: stability (Westravelle)
slides.notes: Their late-stage tablet work at Westravelle is the natural lead-in to Durnesswick formulation support.

slides.title: Don't confuse them with Corvenlith
bullets: Corvenlith Therapeutics is a different company
Quenverell and Durnesswick client; no corporate link to Corvenlea
Always check the client identity bridge before merging accounts

slides.title: How to run a cross-sell review
bullets: Pull the account from the client identity bridge, not one CRM
List service lines bought and not bought
Agree one introduction per quarter with the owning firm
Log the outcome in the cross-sell matrix

slides.title: Support from head office
bullets: Client identity bridge maintained by the integration team
Cross-sell white-space matrix for top accounts
Joint proposal templates in the group template

slides.title: Contacts
bullets: Sofia Lindervik, Integration Director
BD leads in each firm
